title: 5 Surprising Health Benefits of Quercetin You Need to Know
abstract:
# 5 Surprising Health Benefits of Quercetin You Need to Know  
[Quercetin](https://www.jinfiniti.com/category/supplements/quercetin/).  
Did you know a powerful plant compound is working silently in many foods you eat daily?  
Quercetin gives fruits and vegetables their vibrant colors and offers remarkable health benefits. Research shows this flavonoid does far more than just add color to your plate.  
You’ve likely consumed quercetin throughout your life without realizing its potential. Science now reveals it helps fight inflammation and may even support longevity.  
Let’s explore five surprising benefits of quercetin that might change how you view your daily nutrition choices and wellness routine.
## What is Quercetin and Where Can I Find It?  
Quercetin is a naturally occurring plant pigment. It is part of a larger group of compounds known as flavonoids—specifically, flavonols.  
Your body values quercetin primarily for its antioxidant properties. This means it helps protect your cells from damage caused by harmful molecules called free radicals.  
While it’s present in many plants, it’s usually not in its pure form. Instead, it’s commonly bound to sugars, forming compounds called glycosides, which your body breaks down during digestion to absorb the active form.
### Top Food Sources of Quercetin  
The average daily intake of quercetin can vary quite a bit. In typical Western diets, people consume around 4–40 mg daily, but those eating a produce-rich diet may reach 100 mg or more.  
Interestingly, factors like food variety and how it’s grown can impact how much quercetin is actually present. For instance, one studyshowed that organic tomatoes had 79% more quercetin than conventional ones.[1](#1ab56d1d-6f7c-4d44-b550-4d769ecd334f)  
Here’s a quick look at some top sources:

Other good sources include citrus fruits, tomatoes, asparagus, cauliflower, cabbage, and herbs like dill, cilantro, and lovage.
